title: Sprint compression playbook: Hosted API & Model Catalog quarterly consolidation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Create a playbook to compress the quarterly roadmap delivery window for Hosted API and Model Catalog work without increasing regression risk. Scope includes alignment of commit lanes, standard canary timing, contingency hedges for capacity/latency, and a lightweight acceptance checklist for feature readiness.

Why now: Recent quarters show elongated handoffs between model onboarding, runtime validation, and hosted rollout. This increases time-to-commit and blocks cross-functional teams. A focused playbook will shorten the runway while preserving quality (SLOs, model QA), and give PMs/Eng/Design a repeatable pattern for compression and rollback.

Success criteria:
- Mean cross-team handoff time between model onboard -> hosted canary reduced by 30% within one quarter.
- No increase in P1 regressions attributable to compressed schedules during pilot tranches.
- Clear owner for each commit lane with documented contingency triggers and automated fallbacks.

Deliverables:
1) Sprint Compression Playbook doc (confluence): checklist, timelines, staging matrix.
2) Canary window standard operating procedure and guardrails for model swaps.
3) Runway dashboard slice in Console (latency/cost per commit lane) to monitor compression impact.
4) Pilot with two feature lanes (one Hosted API feature, one Model Catalog onboarding) during the next cycle.
updates: 2025-11-05: Ticket created by Aisha. Initial outline and problem statement added. Requested FYI from Eng leads (runtime, infra) and Design.
2025-11-06: Stakeholder sync — Evan, Priya (Design), Mateo (Runtime), and Sasha (SRE). Agreed scope to limit pilot to two lanes to validate hypothesis before broad roll-out.

2025-11-07: Trade-offs noted in meeting: compressing schedule will require stricter pre-rollout gating (QA signoffs, automated smoke tests) and slightly larger canary capacity reserve. Eng estimates ~15% temporary capacity hedge for pilot (ENG-2841).

2025-11-08: Decision: standard canary window = 48h with 4-hour health sampling; automated rollback triggers defined for latency spike > 30% or error-rate > 2x baseline. Action: ENG to add health hooks (ENG-3302).

2025-11-09: Design sent a lightweight UX checklist for hosted endpoint launch: messaging for 'model variant' rollouts, failure states, and customer-facing timeline. Link to artifact: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SC-Compression-UX

2025-11-10: PM review: prioritize pilot lanes — (1) text-generation endpoint A/B rollout, (2) new quantized model onboarding flow. Allocation: 2 engineers full-time for 2 sprints, SRE on-call for pilot window.

2025-11-11: Risk log added: potential quality regressions for edge prompt distributions; mitigation: focused eval suite run daily during canary and auto-block on degradation > 5% across top-10 prompt set.

2025-11-12: Playbook draft complete. Next: schedule pilot kickoff (2025-11-18), link PR with runtime changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5826, and create console dashboard slice ticket (ENG-4129).

Pilot lanes executed and dashboard shows handoff time reduction >= 30%
No P1 regressions directly attributed to compressed rollout during pilot
Contingency hedges and rollback triggers tested end-to-end
